content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato pie is a baked dish whose base is a smooth puree of sweet potatoes mixed with eggs, milk, and spices, topped with a golden crust of pastry. It is popular in North America and Europe as a comforting autumn dessert.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes (batata) are richer in beta‑carotene than regular potatoes, giving the pie its bright orange hue.
The classic recipe emerged in the United States in the early 1920s and quickly became a family favorite.
In many regions the filling is spiced with cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg for a warm aromatic flavor.
The pie can be made with traditional pastry or a gluten‑free crust using oat or almond flour.
Sweet potatoes contain more fiber and vitamin A than regular potatoes.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Provides complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs give lasting satiety and help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Antioxidants in sweet potatoes protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to eggs, dairy, or nuts if they are added to the crust.

items.title: High natural sugar
items.content: Sweet potatoes are naturally sweet; people monitoring glucose should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The pie is calorie‑dense due to pastry and cream; moderation is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pie warm, often with a dollop of whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream. Cut into portions and keep refrigerated for up to 3 days, reheating in the oven before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Allow the pie to cool completely, then cover tightly with plastic wrap and store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 2 months.
